# The REGISTERED verb surface, vendored so the skill-grant gates can expand
# tool_grants without a live database.
#
# Format: <verb id><TAB><adapter id><TAB><adapter runtime>
#
# Provenance: captured 2026-07-27 from the Classical Visas tenant
# (cv-boltrig-postgres-1, database cvboltrig), joining verbs to verb_bindings to
# adapters. Refresh with: python scripts/refresh_verb_surface.py
#
# WHY THE RUNTIME COLUMN. An adapter with runtime `mcp` is a CONSUMED server: its
# tool surface is chosen by the far side and returned from tools/list, so it can
# grow between deploys with no commit in this repo. That is what makes a wildcard
# over it selection-by-upper-bound rather than a selection. Every other runtime
# ships its verbs from code here, so a wildcard expands to a set we authored.
#
# The namespace cannot be derived from the adapter id (`memory-tickets` serves
# `ticket.*`, `browser-cli` serves `browser.*`), and it cannot be derived from the
# filesystem either: builtin adapters bootstrap from scattered modules
# (boltrig.config.control_plane, boltrig.memory.adapter), not one registry, so
# globbing boltrig/adapters/builtin/ wrongly marks `control` and `memory` as
# consumed. That was tried and the gate went red on two false positives. The
# binding row is the only honest source.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. [2026] VJS-COUNTY (SUBMISSION-2026-07-27-123842) CP1
# orders a gate expanding every shipped skill's tool_grants against the FULL
# registered verb set. A gate that can only run where a database is reachable is
# a gate that silently skips, which this repo has already been bitten by (~156
# tests skip when BOLTRIG_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset). So it is vendored.
#
# THE TRAP THIS FILE IS IN. A vendored snapshot goes stale, and staleness is what
# CP1 exists to catch: the 2026-07-24 wildcard fix narrowed ops/opbox to eight
# verbs written against the opbox KERNEL door (noun-first, `opbox.matter.list`)
# while the tenant runs the FRONTEND door (verb-first, `opbox.list_matters`).
# Zero of the eight resolve. The skill has been inert since the outage was
# "fixed" and nothing could have said so. Treat a dead-grant failure as evidence
# about the SKILL until a refresh proves it is evidence about the SURFACE.
#
# NATIVE TARGETS. A verb may bind to a kernel-native target (`native:questions`)
# that has no adapters row, so this MUST be a left join: an inner join silently
# dropped chat.ask_user (196 of 197) and the dead-grant gate then reported a false
# positive against a verb that exists. Native targets are recorded with runtime
# `native` and are definitionally not consumed - the kernel authors them.
